title: The ascension (Acts 1:6–11)
hook: he's lifted out of sight, and two men ask why they're staring at the sky

segments.voice: Yesterday, breakfast on the beach: a charcoal fire and three questions. Your line was three denials, three loves. Who got a fresh start from you? Day seventy-four.

You know the moment at the airport, or the train platform. Someone you love walks through the gate, turns, waves, and is gone. And you stand there. You keep looking at the spot where they were, long after there's nothing to see. Now go to the Mount of Olives, just outside Jerusalem. Acts says that after the empty tomb Jesus kept appearing to his friends for forty days. On the last of them, they ask him the question they've been carrying all along: is this the moment you restore the kingdom to Israel? He says the timing isn't theirs to know. Then, as they watch, he's lifted up, and a cloud takes him out of their sight. And they stand there. Staring at the sky.
screen: `WAVING AT THE GATE.` → `FORTY DAYS.` → `A CLOUD TAKES HIM.`

segments.voice: Just before he goes, Jesus gives them a map, and it turns out to be the map of the whole book of Acts: "ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judaea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth." Jerusalem first, then the countryside, then the neighbors nobody liked, then everywhere. That's the order the story will travel. Then he's gone, and they're still looking up, and suddenly two men in white are standing beside them. In the King James Bible: "Ye men of Galilee, why stand ye gazing up into heaven?" It's almost funny. The biggest moment of their lives, and the first thing heaven says is, why are you still standing here? The men promise he'll come back the same way he went. And then the disciples walk back down the hill to Jerusalem to wait, and to pray. Luke is the only writer who tells this scene in detail, at the end of his Gospel and again at the start of Acts. Christians have never read it as a trip into outer space. The cloud is an old sign in the Bible of God's presence, and the churches say, in the words of the old creeds, that he ascended into heaven and is seated at the right hand of the Father: Jesus taken fully into God's presence, and not gone for good. Christians differ on how literally to picture the rising itself, and the text doesn't explain how it looked. Many churches keep Ascension Day forty days after Easter, so it always falls on a Thursday. But the heart of the story is the question. Stop staring. Go.
screen: `JERUSALEM, THEN THE ENDS OF THE EARTH.` · `WHY STAND YE GAZING?` · `A CLOUD MEANS GOD IS NEAR.` · `FORTY DAYS AFTER EASTER.` · then, large: `STOP STARING. GO.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: look up, then look around. If you can, go to a window or step outside. For the first part, just look up. Sky, ceiling, clouds, whatever's there. Let it be big. If you pray, you can let that be your prayer, without words. Then bring your eyes down, slowly, and look around at what's right in front of you: a street, a room, a person, a sink full of dishes. That's where the disciples were sent back to. Notice one thing there that needs you. The bell holds the time.
The ascension. Jesus taken up out of sight, forty days after Easter, and his friends sent back down the hill.
Your line: stop staring. go. Today, when you catch yourself waiting for a sign, do the next small thing in front of you instead. Tomorrow, wind and fire. Day seventy-four.

howItsDone: Many churches celebrate Ascension Day on the Thursday forty days after Easter, and Christians confess in the Apostles' and Nicene Creeds that Jesus ascended into heaven and is seated at the right hand of the Father.

fork.setup: you're one of the disciples. he's just been taken up into a cloud. the sky is empty. what do you do?

go back to Jerusalem to wait and pray.

fork.reveal: they stare until two men in white ask why. then they walk back down to Jerusalem to wait, as he told them.

original.note: Greek: a taking up. Luke uses it for his being received up, and Greek-speaking churches name the feast with it.

trapdoor: what you thought: Jesus floats off into space.
what it means: he's taken into God's presence, and the first thing heaven says to his friends is, why are you still staring? go.
what a scholar hears: only Luke narrates it in detail (Luke 24 and Acts 1), and the cloud echoes the cloud of God's presence in Exodus and at the transfiguration.

notes: Location: Acts 1:12 says they returned from 'the mount called Olivet'; the script places the scene there.

Ascension Day on the fortieth day after Easter (a Thursday); some churches move the observance to the following Sunday. Not mentioned.
